reply_text:
㊣ ("the only thing that can be trusted ... is this comparator") Agreed: no more questions for you. The loop is: run the rows; on an error, use the comparator, cold; fix the port until it matches Lean. I've written that into the park reminder and into my saved memory.

㊟ ("code that you said was compliant with Lean") You're right to question it. The 20 rows in Rob's main were accepted because their behaviour matched native Lean on preregistered inputs and their instance choices matched. Most of them were never compared with Lean term by term, and the comparator didn't exist when they were accepted. So "compliant" meant "behaves the same on the tested inputs", which is weaker than what you're asking for now.

㊯ (comparator work) I've sent codex-23 two jobs (`invoke-…32776`):
1. **Make the comparator properly cold.** Add a `--cold` option that deletes the whole compiled cache before capturing, because warm captures gave different results this morning.
2. **Audit the 20 accepted rows with it.** Dump Lean's terms where they're missing, capture each row cold in its own worktree, and compare. The results go to `AUDIT-20.md`, listing per row how many nodes match, differ or weren't produced, and the first real difference. Any row with a real difference goes back into the fix loop, including what's already in Rob's main.

㊢ (in progress) Also running: stop C (codex-31, the `(← e)` elaboration), atEnd (codex-19, the single-path type check) and epsilonInfo's cold acceptance (`bg-…795`).
